book.t: In the Hebrew text 2:28-32 is 3:1-5, and 3:1-21 is 4:1-21.

1:1.t: Joel's date is uncertain. The book describes a terrible locust plague as a warning of the day of the LORD.

1:4.t: "Gnawing locust ... swarming locust ... creeping locust ... stripping locust": the KJV's "palmerworm ... locust ... cankerworm ... caterpiller". These may be four kinds of locust or four stages of its growth.

2:25.t: "Gnawing locust ... swarming locust ... creeping locust ... stripping locust": the KJV's "palmerworm ... locust ... cankerworm ... caterpiller". These may be four kinds of locust or four stages of its growth.

2:20.t: "The Dead Sea ... the Mediterranean Sea": the KJV's "the east sea ... the utmost sea". "Surely He has done great things": the KJV reads "because he hath done great things", referring to the invader.

2:23.t: "Because He is faithful": the KJV's "moderately"; the Hebrew litsdaqah means "in righteousness". It can also be read "the teacher of righteousness".

3:2.t: "The Valley of Jehoshaphat": Jehoshaphat means "the LORD judges".

3:12.t: "The Valley of Jehoshaphat": Jehoshaphat means "the LORD judges".

3:11.t: "Assemble": the KJV's source text adds a marginal note to this verse, not part of the verse.

3:18.t: "The valley of acacias": the KJV's "the valley of Shittim".

3:21.t: The KJV's source text adds a marginal note to this verse ("that"), not part of the verse.

2:13.t: "Tear your heart and not your garments": true repentance is inward, not merely outward ritual. "Gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love" (Hebrew chesed): a quotation of Exodus 34:6.

2:28.t: "I will pour out My Spirit on all people" (Hebrew kol basar, "all flesh"): not only on prophets and kings, but on men and women, young and old, servants and free. Peter quoted this passage on the day of Pentecost to explain the coming of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:16-21). Paul quotes verse 32, "Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved", in Romans 10:13, applying the name of the LORD to Jesus.

3:10.t: "Beat your plowshares into swords": the reverse of Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4:3. The nations prepare for a war they cannot win.
